title: night-pulse-quiet-rollout-ops-announce-draft
content:
Purpose:
- Short internal announcement & crib for night shift engineers for a low-risk, quiet rollout (tiered feature flag) across a small subset of Dedicated clusters.
- Provide slack templates, escalation chains, quick checklist. This is a personal scratchpad — keep it short and skimmable.

Background/context (one-liner):
- We’re enabling feature-flagged routing fallback for model-variant B on dedicated-west-2 fleets (canary 3% → 10% over 2 hours) to validate lower-latency kernel selection. No schema changes, no client-facing API changes.
- Goal: validate steady-state p99 latency and error rate impact before scaling.

Rollout window:
- Night window: 23:00 - 02:30 PT (low traffic). Start: 23:15. Estimated 2hr ramp + 30m observation.
- If anything looks off, abort at first safe breakpoint (rollback to flag-off).

Audience:
- Primary: oncall SREs (night), dedicated infra owners, serving-runtime lead on-call.
- Secondary: product-hosted-api + support (heads-up).

Quick checklist for night oncall (sticky):
- Pre-start (15m before):
  - Confirm pager rotation and contactability.
  - Open pagerless monitoring dashboard (link in linked_artifacts) and enable live tail for router logs.
  - Ensure hotfix branch & rollback playbook link open.
  - Notify #infra-deploys with 10m warning (template below).
- Start (T+0):
  - Flip flag to 3% for west-2 dedicated pool via admin UI (screenshot saved in Confluence).
  - Verify rolling util across 2 nodes only, watch for error spikes for 10 minutes.
- Ramp (T+15, T+45):
  - If p50/p95 stable and error rate < baseline + 0.1%, increase to 10% at T+15.
  - Continue observation for 30–45 minutes.
- Observe (T+90):
  - If metrics good, leave at 10% and post short summary in #infra-deploys and DM product-hosted-api leads.
- Complete (T+150):
  - Mark rollout complete, open short rollback window of 60 minutes in case of delayed regressions.

Abort/rollback criteria (be conservative):
- Sustained p95 increase > 200ms above baseline for 10 continuous minutes.
- Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute for 5 minutes or any HTTP 5xx surge tied to this routing path.
- Any client-facing alerts from support or automated SLA triggers.
- Unusual memory/GPU pressure on nodes serving the canary.

Escalation chain (fast):
- Night oncall (primary) -> Pager -> Diego Morales (infra lead) -> Hannah Lee (serving-runtime) -> Eleanor Park (author/owner) -> CTO if unresolved after 30m with impact.
- If pager misses, DM on-call secondary and ping #infra-execs.

Slack templates (short):
- 10m warning (post to #infra-deploys):
  "Heads-up: starting quiet rollout for routing fallback (model B) on dedicated-west-2 at 23:15 PT. Canary 3% → 10% over 2hr with 30m observation. Oncall: @night-oncall. See playbook: Confluence link. Ping here with visible regressions."
- Abort message (if rollback):
  "Rollback: Aborting quiet rollout for routing fallback due to sustained p95 degradation. Flipping flag off now. Oncall will follow up with root cause notes. Contact @Diego for immediate triage."
- Success message: 
  "Complete: Quiet rollout finished and stable at 10% for 90 minutes. No SLA regressions observed. Will keep a 60-minute watch window. Summary and metrics in Confluence."

Possible questions & suggested answers (for quick comms):
- Q: Will this affect user-facing latency?
  A: Low probability — canary is tiny subset and we have automated rollback at small thresholds. We’ll pause if p95 moves meaningfully.
- Q: Why run at night?
  A: Minimal traffic reduces blast radius and lets us collect steady-state tails for tail-latency analysis.
- Q: Any change to token billing or model outputs?
  A: No changes to responses or billing. Just routing-level kernel selection and scheduling tweaks.

Notes-to-self (things to double-check before start):
- Confirm dashboards are pulling from west-2 dedicated cluster metrics (not aggregated across regions).
- Verify alerts tied to this rollout are suppressed from noisy auto-reminders (we still need actionable pages).
- Pre-cache small prompt set to validate end-to-end latency quickly (link to prompts file in Confluence).
- Upload short GIF/screenshots for docs for future runbook.

Post-rollout follow-up items (if successful):
- 1) Short postmortem-freeform note in Confluence with p50/p95/error deltas and recording.
- 2) Add brief blurb to biweekly infra notes summarizing the run.
- 3) If stable for 48h, propose progressive rollout to 30% with same night-window safety net.

Open questions / unknowns (callouts):
- Are there any scheduled backups or maintenance windows in west-2 during our window? (check infra calendar)
- Does the dedicated cluster autoscaler behave differently at 3% traffic? Need to verify none triggered scale events.

Links to quick artifacts: JIRA INFR-4379, Confluence playbook (linked above), Slack thread for past canary notes.

Finish: this is a working scratchpad; share with Diego/Hannah for quick sanity check and then I’ll convert into a short #infra-deploys announcement and a one-pager in Confluence.

- Attach screenshot of admin-UI flag toggle to Confluence
- Draft 10m/abort/success slack posts and save to templates snippet library

-- Eleanor

(End of scratchpad)
